Blog


September 10, 2026


## What’s New in Quindar v0.37


Quindar v0.37 brings meaningful improvements across planning, flight dynamics, and day-to-day operator workflows.


This release is centered on a simple outcome: giving mission teams more visibility, more control, and more efficient ways to manage complex operations. From smarter fleet scheduling to automated stationkeeping and a redesigned navigation experience, v0.37 helps teams move faster while staying mission-ready.


## Better fleet planning and contact scheduling


Planning workflows are only as effective as the clarity they provide. In v0.37, Quindar adds new capabilities that make it easier to work through dense schedules and focus on the contacts that matter most.


Teams can now filter contact metadata directly on the timeline using fields such as ground station provider and antenna. That makes it easier to review large scheduling plans across multiple providers, antennas, and assets without losing time scanning for the right information.


Quindar also introduces preset timeframes for fleet scheduling. Operators can quickly choose common scheduling windows like 1 day, 3 days, or 7 days, or select a custom range when a mission requires more flexibility. The result is a faster, more intuitive scheduling workflow with fewer invalid submissions and less manual setup.


Together, these updates strengthen Quindar’s role as mission management software built for modern space operations. Mission teams get a clearer common operating picture and more control over how planning decisions are made.


## More flexible task sequencing for operators


Operators can now append or prepend tasks from more areas of the product, including Requests, Draft Queues, and Contact Tasks. This gives teams more flexibility in how they sequence work based on timing, priority, and mission context. Added confirmation behavior for critical tasks also helps prevent accidental insertion of high-impact actions.


This update supports more flexible operational planning by allowing teams to add tasks before or after existing work depending on mission needs, operational context, and urgency. For teams managing time-sensitive workflows, that added control can remove friction and make day-to-day execution more adaptable.


## Automated stationkeeping for scalable orbit maintenance


Quindar now supports stationkeeping using semi-major axis as the control metric. Operators can define stationkeeping thresholds for each spacecraft, and every time updated OD and propagation data is available, Quindar automatically determines if an spacecraft is expected to violate its configured stationkeeping limits.


When a violation is detected, Quindar can generate stationkeeping maneuver options, select a maneuver based on fuel usage and ignition timing, and package the required maneuver files into a spacecraft task for uplink.


This is an important step forward for teams managing growing fleets and increasingly complex operational demands. Instead of relying on manual monitoring alone, operators can use Quindar to identify issues earlier, streamline maneuver planning, and support more resilient orbit maintenance workflows.


## Built for mission-ready operations


Taken together, the updates in v0.37 reflect the direction of the Quindar platform: more automation-first workflows, more operational clarity, and better support for the realities of modern space operations.


Quindar is the future of mission management, and releases like v0.37 continue to strengthen the visibility, control, and resiliency mission teams need to operate with confidence.


If you are already using Quindar, v0.37 delivers immediate improvements across planning, flight dynamics, and operator efficiency. If you are evaluating how to modernize mission operations, these updates offer a clear view into the kind of mission-ready workflows the platform is designed to support.
